chapter: Building the band: Dave Duncan, Denver and Rene Hall
title: Travelling in two cars and the New Mexico commercial permit
summary: With instruments on the car roofs, the band is stopped at a port of entry and made to buy a twenty-five-dollar permit.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: We had two cars and carried the instruments on top of the car. That finally one time got us into trouble. New Mexico had a law that if you were doing commercial work, you had to have a commercial license--

Sure enough. I'll never forget, Herbert Scott, this fellow that I told you we got from Bessie Smith, he was just so elated that he was a musician, of his job and the band and he was just going to let everybody know what his job is, so we stopped at the port of entry once and this guy went in--I think Scotty--I didn't go, I sent Scotty or somebody told me I better go on in, Scotty was so long and the man looked out and said, what's all that on top of the car, (inaudible). They guy just let him talk. We'll be playing so and so and so and so, and so he said you're going to have to buy a license. So they got me then and I went out and said

I don't have the money for that and I said some kind of tale like it wasn't commercial, so the guy said he would follow us; I guess it wasn't too far away where we were going to play and he said I'll follow you and see what you're doing. So at night, the highway patrol came there and they didn't make me buy no state license, but they made me buy a permit. (Inaudible).
How much was the permit; do you remember?
It was very little, it was big money then though. I think it was about twenty five dollars. But if they made us buy a license for that commercial thing it would have been a hundred dollars.
I had to pay ten dollars to go into Colorado, with my bus.
